links.outcome: Robustness of general-purpose vs medical LLMs to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations on DiagnosisQA and MedQA
links.effect: Robustness differences between domain-specific and general-purpose models were mixed and model-dependent; some DS models were among the most robust, and strong GP baselines stayed competitive. Sensitivity to rephrasing is described as a risk.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that robustness differences between domain-specific (DS) models are mixed and highly model-dependent, i.e., domain specialization does not consistently improve or reduce robustness to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations.

unlisted_practices: NLI-based semantic verification with LLM-as-a-judge and clinical expert audit to filter meaning-preserving prompt variations
Semantic stability metrics (MVS, confidence variation, worst-case instability) for LLM robustness

screen.reason: Evaluates semantic stability and robustness of general-purpose and medical LLMs across prompt reformulations using benchmark datasets (DiagnosisQA and MedQA); does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
